target: https://admin.mikbill.pro (public demo). Writes were on MCPTEST records only (users 888, device types 28 to 30, device 350 and 351). All were removed or soft-deleted afterwards.

notes: All values are strings. The req_* flags say which ticket fields the category requires. Names are translation keys such as 'other', 'connection', 'internet_does_not_work'; one custom name was Cyrillic.
No totalCount. 4 staff on the demo. The session's own login (demo, stuffid 2) is in the list.

mb_get_user_devices.finding: The parameter is useruid. With uid (as the upstream README and the first fixture used) Mikbill returns an empty {} even when the user has devices. That is why the earlier fixture had no record fields.
mb_get_user_devices.response: {success: true, error: 0, data: [device rows]}; an empty list is {success: true, data: []}
mb_get_user_devices.also_in: getuserdatambp data.devices has the same rows.

mb_add_user_device.response: {success: true, error: 0}. The device id is not returned; read it with mb_get_user_devices.
mb_add_user_device.verified: The device appeared in getuserdevicesbyuid (devid 350 and 351) with the right devtypeid and devtypename.

errors: With devid alone: {success: false, error: 1, errortext: 'Абонент не найден'} (subscriber not found). useruid is required.
mb_delete_user_device.verified: After the call the user's device list was empty.

mb_delete_dev_type.finding: SILENT NO-OP with devtypeid: Mikbill answers {success: true, data: [{error: 0, delete_list: '1'}]} and deletes nothing, with or without devices. The UI's parameter is delete_list, which really deletes. The earlier contract runs used devtypeid and never checked the list, so they leaked one MCPTEST device type per run (21 to 28 were found and removed).
mb_delete_dev_type.in_use: With delete_list and a device still using the type: {success: false, error: 1, errortext: 'Невозможно удалить тип устройства так как оно все еще используется'}. After the device was removed the delete worked and the type left the list.
mb_delete_dev_type.audit: Every other delete in the contract suite was checked against the demo for leftovers: sectors, switches, switch types, packets, IP pools, NAS, real IPs, settlements, neighborhoods and lanes were all really deleted. Only device types had this problem.

mb_restore_user.summary: A soft-deleted user (state 4, deletedtable 1) is restored by enableusersmulti alone, or by vkluserflex alone when a tariff should be assigned.

verified: soft delete (deluserflex), then enableusersmulti: state 4 to 1, status normal, deletedtable 0, same gid and tariff.
disconnect (otkluserflex) then delete (deluserotklflex) then enableusersmulti: also back to state 1, not to the disconnected state 3.
enableusersmulti on a merely disconnected user (state 3): state 1.
A user whose gid was 0 (scheduled tariff change) stayed on gid 0 (tariff 'Error') after enableusersmulti.
From the deleted state (4) directly: state 1, status normal, deletedtable 0, gid changed from 0 to 1 (tariff assigned). No separate enable step is needed.
The deposit dropped by 1 on that call (the tariff's first daily fee), so assigning a tariff can charge.
From a disconnected state (3) it also works (verified earlier).
errors: On an active user it fails with MSG_ERROR_ABONENT_DUPLICATE_LOGIN (error 2): it only works from the deleted or disconnected state.

mb_restore_user.tool_design: uid required, gid and itog_summa optional. Without gid: enableusersmulti. With gid: vkluserflex with itog_summa (default 0) and type_list 2. The user must be deleted (state 4) or the tool returns precondition_failed. The state is read back and the tool fails if the user is still deleted.
